title: LP2-32: grid sums and the 2016 message file
question: Do the first row, first column and central 5x5 perimeter of a row-major 11x11 grid match the 2016 image dimensions and payload length?
summary: Reproduces sums 563, 569 and 1136 under a specified grid layout. These equal the preserved image dimensions and payload bytes; significance and intent remain untested.

scope.representation: All 121 alphabet runes in archived LP2-32 order, stripped of separators and filled left-to-right into 11 rows of 11; Gematria Primus prime values.
scope.procedure: Sum first row, first column, and the 16 distinct cells on the central 5x5 perimeter; compare with JPEG header dimensions and payload bytes. Report all 49 contiguous 5x5 perimeter sums.
scope.parameters: One row-major 11x11 layout; central rows and columns 4–8 one-based; corners counted once; 49 possible 5x5 positions; no rotations or reversals.
scope.exclusions: Alternative layouts, other pages, extraction/signature retesting, null-model simulations, image identity, intentionality and decryption.

finding: First row=563, first column=569, central perimeter=1136. Image header=563x569; preserved extraction=1136 bytes. The central position is the only 1136 perimeter among the 49 tested positions.
limitations: Chosen exploratory layout and measurements. Numerical equality does not establish rarity or an intended connection. The 11x11 grid differs from printed lines. Human review pending.
next_steps: Specify any comparison corpus or randomized model before assessing rarity; record layout changes as separate family variants.

family.title: Grid sums and message-file measurements
family.question: Which specified grid sums match preserved message-file measurements?

review.reviewer: Codex; independent flat-index sums from page JSON and JPEG header check; human review pending

reproduction.environment: Python 3.12 standard library. Original images/message-2016.jpg must be downloaded separately (26,342 bytes; checksum in image-input manifest). Independent check: python experiments/records/lp2-32-message-grid/check.py

visuals.caption: Top: the tested 11×11 arrangement, with first row and column in pale blue and central perimeter in dark blue. Bottom: the 5×5 block with prime values. Sum the 16 dark cells once; exclude the nine interior cells.
